cards.title: DOSE CORRECTION · 2026-08-25
cards.text:
Brooks: the dose is TWO gummies before bed, not three. All nine re-rendered.

Root cause: the mechanism bible said 'Three before bed with a full glass of water' as canon, so every downstream ad inherited it. MOT-WRONGEND-VSL-01/script-v2.md had already flagged the contradiction inline (product doc said 3 before bed but also 1-month at 2/day) and it was never resolved. Sixty in a bottle at two a day is a clean thirty-day supply, which is what the one-month positioning always implied.

FIXED: the mechanism bible (with a dated correction note), plus the copy docs for all three concepts in this run.

cards.title: THE THREE VISUALS
cards.text:
V1 STOMACH. Week 0 swollen and distended, walls stretched taut, dull lifeless grey-mauve, no glow. Week 2 less swollen, colour partway back, faint glow. Week 4 normal size, warm vivid pink, lit from within. The dull-to-glowing colour arc carries this one; Week 2 and Week 4 sit close in size, so the light does the storytelling.

V2 BELLY. Week 0 hugely distended and tight. Week 2 noticeably reduced. Week 4 flat and calm. Ribcage and hip width pinned identical across all three on purpose, so only the abdomen changes. That is both the mechanism and the compliance position.

V3 COLON. Week 0 congested, loops bulging into tight pockets, densely packed, dull. Week 2 partway clear, some pockets still holding, glow starting. Week 4 clear and open, warm pink lit from within. Most visceral, most literal, likely the strongest scroll-stopper and the most likely to draw a policy look.

cards.title: THE 3D-LOOK LAW
cards.text:
The standing rule bans the 3D-render look and calls it a hard regenerate.

That rule exists so frames which should read as photographed never come back as CGI. It does not apply here: an anatomical organ cannot be photographed, the reference is itself a 3D render, and Brooks specified 3D models for this concept directly.

Noted so nobody later reads these as a law breach.

cards.title: SHARED PRIMARY TEXT · all nine
cards.text:
Nobody shows you this part, so here it is.

A GLP-1 works by slowing digestion down. That is the point, and it works. What nobody mentions is that the slowdown does not stop at your stomach. It reaches all the way to your colon.

Your colon is a muscle, and a muscle only moves when something tells it to. That signal is a short-chain fatty acid called butyrate, and you do not make it yourself. The bacteria in your colon make it out of the fiber that reaches them.

Slow everything down and less reaches them. The colony thins out. Butyrate drops. The muscle gets a weaker signal, so less moves, so even less reaches them tomorrow. It feeds on itself, and the medication holds that first slowdown in place, which is what keeps the loop shut.

That is the week 0 picture. Congested, stalled, and getting a little tighter every week you leave it.

Motilli works on the two things that have to happen together. Concentrated celery juice standardized for a real dose of apigenin, which barely absorbs into your bloodstream and so stays down in the colon where the problem is, calming the lining and shifting the balance back toward the butyrate makers. Plus a fine soluble fiber that feeds those bacteria specifically, without the coarse bulk that leaves you more distended than when you started.

Rebuild the place, then feed what grows there. Every product in your drawer did one, the other, or neither.

Days 1 to 4 are quiet, because this is not a laxative and nothing is being forced. The first normal, non-cramping movement usually lands around day five. It fills in from there.

None of this touches your weight loss. Weight loss lives in the brain and the appetite, which is the dial the medication turns. This lives in the colon and the bacteria in it. Because they are separate systems, you rebuild the gut and you stay on the medication.

Two gummies before bed with a full glass of water. Third-party tested, lab results posted.
